item: Characteristic-2 spectral-curve bridge (paper I29+I32+I35): over F2-bar, with D = diag(theta) distinct and G_D(X) = [s^q t^q] per_k(X+sI+tD) = [s^q t^q] det(X+sI+tD), grad G_D(X) = 0 forces the adjugate zero scheme Z of the spectral curve C_X = V(det(sI+tD+uX)) to have length >= T = C(q+2,2); conductor gives delta(C_X) >= T; a Severi count plus a fibre count give dim{grad G_D = 0} <= k^2 + k - T. Result: quadratic codimension of the critical locus of a linear-degree permanent projection.
item_type: F5 (change of representation: permanent coefficient -> determinantal pencil mod 2 -> plane spectral curve)
lean_status_why: The first half of the bridge (grad G_D = 0 implies normalization defect >= C(q+2,2)) is formalized as in the paper (gradient_forces_normalization_defect / critical_normalization_defect via vanishing adjugate coefficients). The second half replaces the cited CHT2023 Severi dimension and the Hilbert-scheme fibre bound by a char-2 Frobenius square-form delta bound plus a transcendence-degree parameter count, giving a weaker codimension (>= floor(C(q+2,2)/18) instead of >= T - k) that still yields the paper's final constant.
lean_gaps: Different route for the dimension count: spectral_effective_bound uses exists_squareForm (f = a^2 + x b^2 + y c^2 + xy d^2 in char 2), Conductor.normalization_length_le_half and CurveFamily.half_curve_parameter_bound (18 n + T <= 9 (k+1)(k+2)). The paper uses the CHT2023 char-2 Severi dimension theorem (cited, unproved) plus dim Hilb^N(C) <= N via the row-adjugate subscheme. The Lean therefore does not depend on CHT2023.

Weaker intermediate statement: Lean bounds ringKrullDim(K[X_ij]/gradientIdeal) <= (k+1)^2 - floor(C(q+2,2)/18) for matrix size k+1; the paper gives dim <= k^2 + k - T for size k. Codimension >= floor(T/18) (about k^2/324) instead of >= T - k (about k^2/18). The Lean section dimension is sectionSize = floor(C(q+2,2)/18) instead of the paper's floor(k^2/100). explicit_constant still reaches m^3/(5529600 e), the same constant as the paper. We did not trace how the slack is absorbed.

Algebraic rather than geometric formulation: Krull dimension of a quotient of MvPolynomial over any infinite perfect field of characteristic 2 (more general than F2-bar). The spectral curve is the affine monic charpoly of the pencil X.diag(theta) + A, and delta is normalizationDefect := length of (integral closure of AdjoinRoot) / image. The paper uses the projective plane curve C_X and its delta-invariant. Monicity plus separability (distinct_slope_pencil_separable) replace the paper's 'finite flat projection with a distinct-root fibre' lemma.

Char-2 to C transfer: the Lean consumer HasBorderDeterminant.selector_lower_of_critical_dimension accepts the dimension bound over any field K and transfers through the integer family Selector.integralCoefficientFamily (integralCoefficientFamily_specialize, SliceParameters.nonzero_of_gradientDimension). The paper uses a proper family over Spec Z[theta]. Not traced line by line.

Only the PermanentCubic comparator depends on the bridge. BFS from OAI.PermanentBorder.smooth_initial_form_lower_bound (SmoothInitialForm comparator) does NOT reach critical_dimension_effective or spectral_effective_bound: that comparator is the smooth-form (Sheshadri-architecture) branch.

Dominated shares of the 1258-decl proof DAG (data/items/108_lean.json): critical_dimension_effective 0.485, spectral_effective_bound 0.192, gradient_forces_normalization_defect 0.079, critical_normalization_defect 0.056.
No docstrings in the Lean. Text-level analysis only; nothing compiled here. Guo (arXiv:2609.29568v2) reports rebuilding 12 declarations at openai/math commit adc7f12, not fd4aeeb.
comparator_chain_note: PermanentCubic.json: solution_module OAI.Algebra.Determinantal.Main, theorem OAI.PermanentBorder.permanent_cubic_lower_bounds. critical_dimension_effective calls both gradient_forces_normalization_defect (first half of the bridge) and spectral_effective_bound (second half); the list gives both branches. Consumer: permanent_border_cubic_lower_bound feeds the bound into HasBorderDeterminant.selector_lower_of_critical_dimension (ConditionalBound.lean:393). SmoothInitialForm.json (OAI.PermanentBorder.smooth_initial_form_lower_bound) does not depend on the bridge. Paths from BFS over data/items/108_lean.json.

theorem critical_dimension_effective {K : Type u} [Field K] [Infinite K]
    [CharP K 2] [PerfectRing K 2] {k q : ℕ} (hk : 4 ≤ k+1) (hq : 3*q ≤ k)
    (θ : Fin (k+1) → K) (hθ : Function.Injective θ) :
    ringKrullDim (MvPolynomial (Fin (k+1) × Fin (k+1)) K ⧸ gradientIdeal K θ q) ≤
      (((k+1)^2-(q+2).choose 2/18 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) := by

variable [CharP K 2] [CharP L 2] [PerfectRing K 2] [Infinite K] [IsAlgClosed L]

theorem spectral_effective_bound {k : ℕ} (hk : 4 ≤ k+1)
    (θ : Fin (k+1) → K) (hθ : Function.Injective θ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin (k+1)) (Fin (k+1)) L) (T : ℕ)
    (hT : (T : ℕ∞) ≤ normalizationDefect (fun i => algebraMap K L (θ i)) A) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, Algebra.trdeg K (curveCoefficientField (K := K)
      (pencilMatrix (pencilBase (fun i => algebraMap K L (θ i)) A)).det) ≤ (n : Cardinal) ∧
      18*n+T ≤ 9*((k+1)*(k+2)) := by

lean_source.name: OAI.PermanentBorder.Selector.gradient_forces_normalization_defect
lean_source.text:
theorem gradient_forces_normalization_defect {K : Type*}
    [Field K] [Infinite K] [CharP K 2] {k q : ℕ} (hq : 3*q ≤ k)
    (θ : Fin (k+1) → K) (hθ : Function.Injective θ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin (k+1)) (Fin (k+1)) K)
    (hcrit : ∀ ij : Fin (k+1) × Fin (k+1), MvPolynomial.eval
      (fun ab : Fin (k+1) × Fin (k+1) => A ab.1 ab.2)
      (pderiv ij (diagonalCoefficient
        (Matrix.of fun a b => (MvPolynomial.X (a,b) :
          MvPolynomial (Fin (k+1) × Fin (k+1)) K)) (fun i => MvPolynomial.C (θ i)) q)) = 0) :
    let T := -(pencilBase θ A)
    let Q := FractionRing K[X]
    let R := integralClosure K[X] (AdjoinRoot (T.charpoly.map (algebraMap K[X] Q)))
    ((q+2).choose 2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.length K (R ⧸ LinearMap.range
      (normalizationInclusion (Q := Q) T.charpoly T.charpoly_monic).toLinearMap) := by

lean_source.name: OAI.PermanentBorder.AdjugateAlgebra.critical_normalization_defect
lean_source.text:
theorem critical_normalization_defect
    (θ : Fin (k+1) → K) (hθ : Function.Injective θ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin (k+1)) (Fin (k+1)) K) (q : ℕ) (hq : 3*q ≤ k)
    (hcrit : ∀ i j, (((pencilMatrix (pencilBase θ A)).adjugate i j).coeff q).coeff q = 0) :
    let T := -(pencilBase θ A)
    let Q := FractionRing K[X]
    let R := integralClosure K[X] (AdjoinRoot (T.charpoly.map (algebraMap K[X] Q)))
    ((q+2).choose 2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.length K (R ⧸ LinearMap.range
      (normalizationInclusion (Q := Q) T.charpoly T.charpoly_monic).toLinearMap) := by

noncomputable def diagonalCoefficient (M : Matrix I I R) (θ : I → R) (q : ℕ) : R :=
  ((Matrix.of fun i j => C (M i j) : Matrix I I (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) R)) +
    (Matrix.diagonal (fun i => X (0 : Fin 2) + C (θ i)*X 1) : Matrix I I (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) R))).permanent.coeff
    (countIndex q)

noncomputable def gradientIdeal {k : ℕ} (θ : Fin (k+1) → K) (q : ℕ) :
    Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin (k+1) × Fin (k+1)) K) :=
  Ideal.span (Set.range (fun ij => pderiv ij (Selector.diagonalCoefficient
    (Matrix.of fun a b => (MvPolynomial.X (a,b) :
      MvPolynomial (Fin (k+1) × Fin (k+1)) K)) (fun i => MvPolynomial.C (θ i)) q)))

lean_source.name: OAI.PermanentBorder.pencilBase
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def pencilBase (θ : Fin (k+1) → K)
    (A : Matrix (Fin (k+1)) (Fin (k+1)) K) :
    Matrix (Fin (k+1)) (Fin (k+1)) K[X] :=
  (X : K[X]) • (Matrix.diagonal θ).map C + A.map C

lean_source.text:
theorem exists_effective_critical_bound {K : Type} [Field K] [Infinite K]
    [CharP K 2] [PerfectRing K 2] {d : ℕ} (hd : 128 ≤ d) :
    ∃ θ : Fin d → K,
      ringKrullDim (MvPolynomial (Variables d) K ⧸
        Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i => pderiv i
          (Selector.diagonalCoefficient
            (Matrix.of fun a b => (X (a,b) : MvPolynomial (Variables d) K))
            (fun i => C (θ i)) (selectorIndex d))))) ≤
        ((d^2-sectionSize d : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) := by

theorem HasBorderDeterminant.selector_lower_of_critical_dimension
    {K : Type} [Field K] {m n k q d B : ℕ}
    (h : HasBorderDeterminant n (permanentPolynomial m))
    (hk : 0 < k) (hq : q ≤ k) (hr : 2 ≤ k-2*q) (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (hm : 11*k-2*q ≤ m) (θ : Fin k → K)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (MvPolynomial (Variables k) K ⧸
      Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i => pderiv i
        (Selector.diagonalCoefficient
          (Matrix.of fun a b => (X (a,b) : MvPolynomial (Variables k) K))
          (fun i => C (θ i)) q)))) ≤ B)
    (hB : B+(d-1) < k^2) :
    (((k-2*q-1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * ((d-1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) / (4*Real.exp 1) ≤ n := by

theorem exists_selector_affine_projection (k q m : ℕ) (hq : q ≤ k)

    ∃ (b : Variables m → ℂ) (B : Variables m → Variables k → ℂ),
      affineSubstitution b B (permanentPolynomial m) =
        selectorScalar k q • coefficientPolynomial k q θ := by

speedup_targets.statement: Division-free arithmetic circuits computing per_n over C need Omega(n^2 log log n) gates (Ten Advances). Strengthening via the bridge (Guo v2): L_div(per_n) >= (n^2/119790) log2(n/44) for n >= 1936.
speedup_targets.reference: OpenAI, 'Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science' (1 Aug 2026), Ch. 5 'Circuit and Formula Lower Bounds for the Permanent', https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/ten-proofs-oai.pdf; Lean: github.com/openai/ten-proofs Permanent.lean; J. Guo, arXiv:2609.29568v2 (8 Oct 2026).
speedup_targets.status: n^2 log log n: known (model-produced, Lean-certified). n^2 log n: Guo v2, written deduction from 12 machine-checked 108 declarations, not formalized end to end.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Ch. 5 is about 40 pages (pp. 114-153, incl. the formula bound). ten-proofs Permanent.lean has 27,563 lines; the minor-sum critical-locus block (minorSum..., roughly lines 11,284-19,250) is about 8k lines.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Ten Advances Stage 2 needs a degree-d permanent specialization with critical codimension k = Theta(n^2). Its Stage 3 gets that only at bounded degree, via minor sums M_{t,s,d}, power sums and Möbius inclusion-exclusion; the chapter names 'd growing with n' as the next target. The bridge's output exists_effective_critical_bound plus exists_selector_affine_projection gives degree about k/3 with codimension >= floor(C(q+2,2)/18). Feeding it into the slicing lemma (exists_slicedGradient_of_criticalLocus_codimension in ten-proofs) and the Bezout/Baur-Strassen count gives k log(d-1)/3 = Theta(n^2 log n). This replaces the about 8k-line minor-sum block and strengthens the bound.

top5.title: Permanent circuit lower bound (Ten Advances Ch. 5), and the n^2 log n strengthening
top5.argument: The bridge's output (exists_effective_critical_bound with the selector projection) is exactly the input Ten Advances' Stage 2 asks for, at growing degree. top5.title: Cubic symmetric determinantal complexity of the permanent
top5.argument: Exact obstruction match on the permanent side, and the only open problem where the bridge can be used unchanged. What is missing is the symmetric smooth-form bound, a Sheshadri-style variant. Statable with about 40 lines of definitions. Success would be a new theorem obtained by device reuse, still on the permanent.

top5.title: Hafnian/Pfaffian analogue of the bridge
top5.argument: This is the strongest test of whether the device generalises beyond the permanent: haf = Pf mod 2 plays the role of per = det mod 2, and Pfaffian pencils have spectral curves. It needs about 100-200 lines of Pfaffian/hafnian definitions. A positive result would be genuine cross-problem reuse of the mechanism. Low-medium confidence.

top5.title: Sharp char-2 Severi-type bound for determinantal plane curves
top5.argument: Targets the bridge's own second half. The Lean already contains an elementary 18x-weak version (spectral_effective_bound). Sharpening it would remove the paper's reliance on CHT2023. Statable with OAI's normalizationDefect. Payoff is mostly internal.

top5.title: Mignon-Ressayre quadratic bound via the bridge (calibration)
top5.argument: Statable now with OAI's Model. The bridge route should be longer and weaker than MR's Hessian proof, so this is a calibration target where we expect no compression. If a prover nonetheless finds it shorter, that is a red flag for the measurement.
